q: How many points does a tangent to a circle intersect it at? (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
e: A tangent to a circle intersects it at only one point (point of contact).

q: A line intersecting a circle in two points is called a ________. (NCERT)
e: A line intersecting a circle at two distinct points is called a secant.

q: How many parallel tangents can a circle have? (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
e: A circle can have at most two parallel tangents (at opposite ends of a diameter).

q: The common point of a tangent to a circle and the circle is called the ________. (NCERT)
e: The common point is called the point of contact.

q: By Theorem 10.1, the tangent at any point of a circle is ________ to the radius through the point of contact. (NCERT)
e: The tangent is always perpendicular (90°) to the radius at the point of contact.

q: How many tangents can a circle have in total? (JAC PYQ)
e: Since a circle has infinitely many points, it has infinitely many tangents.

q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point lying inside it? (NCERT)
e: Every line through an interior point intersects the circle twice (secant), so 0 tangents.

q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle at a point lying ON the circle?
e: There is one and only one tangent at any point on the circle.

q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from an external point? (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
e: Exactly two tangents can be drawn from an external point to a circle.

q: According to Theorem 10.2, the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are ________. (NCERT)
e: Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.

q: What is the longest chord of a circle called?
e: The diameter (passing through the centre) is the longest chord of a circle.

q: The tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are ________. (NCERT)
e: Interior angles on the same side of the diameter sum to 90° + 90° = 180°, so the tangents are parallel.

q: What is the angle in a semicircle? (JAC PYQ)
e: An angle inscribed in a semicircle is always 90°.

q: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord ________ the chord.
e: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.

q: Equal chords of a circle are ________ from the centre. (JAC PYQ)
e: Equal chords of a circle are equidistant from the centre.

q: When two circles of radii r₁ and r₂ touch externally, the distance d between their centres is:
e: For externally touching circles, d = r₁ + r₂.

q: When two circles touch internally (r₁ > r₂), the distance between their centres is:
e: For internally touching circles, distance between centres = r₁ - r₂.

q: Two circles having the same centre but different radii are called:
e: Circles with the same centre and different radii are concentric circles.

q: What is the sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral?
e: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary (sum = 180°).

q: If PA and PB are two tangents from external point P to a circle with centre O, what property holds for quadrilateral OAPB?
o: It is always a cyclic quadrilateral
e: Since ∠OAP + ∠OBP = 90° + 90° = 180°, OAPB is always a cyclic quadrilateral.

q: How many common tangents can be drawn to two non-intersecting circles lying outside each other (d > r₁ + r₂)? (JAC PYQ)
e: Two direct and two transverse common tangents make a total of 4 common tangents.

q: How many common tangents do two externally touching circles have? (JAC PYQ)
e: Externally touching circles have 3 common tangents (2 direct + 1 at the point of contact).

q: How many common tangents can two internally touching circles have? (JAC PYQ)
e: Internally touching circles have exactly 1 common tangent at their point of contact.

q: How many common tangents can two concentric circles (r₁ ≠ r₂) have?
e: Since the smaller circle lies strictly inside the larger one, there are 0 common tangents.

q: A parallelogram circumscribing a circle is always a ________. (NCERT)
e: In a circumscribing parallelogram, AB + CD = BC + DA => 2AB = 2BC => AB = BC, making it a rhombus.

q: What does the line OP joining centre O to external point P do to ∠APB (angle between the two tangents)?
e: ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP by RHS, so OP bisects ∠APB and ∠AOB.

q: What angle does a tangent PQ make with radius OP at the point of contact P? (JAC PYQ)
e: By Theorem 10.1, ∠OPQ = 90°.

q: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is ________ the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.
e: The central angle is twice the inscribed angle on the remaining arc.

q: Angles in the same segment of a circle are ________.
e: Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.

q: If two tangents to a circle are inclined to each other at 90°, what is the angle between the two radii at the points of contact?
e: Since the central angle and tangent angle sum to 180°, central angle = 180° - 90° = 90°.

q: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and the distance of Q from the centre is 25 cm. Find the radius of the circle. (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
A tangent PQ at a point P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the centre O at a point Q so that OQ = 12 cm. Length PQ is: (NCERT)
e: In right ΔOPQ, PQ = √(12² - 5²) = √119 cm.

q: If tangents PA and PB from a point P to a circle with centre O are inclined to each other at angle of 80°, then ∠POA is equal to: (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
e: ∠AOB = 180° - 80° = 100°. Since OP bisects ∠AOB, ∠POA = 50°.

q: If TP and TQ are the two tangents to a circle with centre O so that ∠POQ = 110°, then ∠PTQ is equal to: (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
Two concentric circles are of radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle. (NCERT / JAC PYQ)
e: Half-chord = √(5² - 3²) = 4 cm. Full chord = 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

q: The length of tangent from point A at distance 13 cm from the centre of a circle is 12 cm. Find the radius of the circle. (JAC PYQ)
The length of tangent drawn from a point 17 cm away from the centre is 15 cm. Find the radius. (JAC PYQ)
From an external point P, two mutually perpendicular tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O. If PA = 5 cm, find AB. (JAC PYQ)
e: ∠APB = 90° and PA = PB = 5 cm. By Pythagoras, AB = √(5² + 5²) = 5√2 cm.

q: What is the distance between two parallel tangents of a circle of radius 3 cm? (CBSE PYQ)
e: Distance between two parallel tangents equals the diameter = 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

q: A tangent PQ of length 12 cm is drawn from a point P to a circle of radius 5 cm. Find the distance OP from the centre O.
Two circles of radii 8 cm and 5 cm touch each other externally. What is the distance between their centres?
e: Distance = r₁ + r₂ = 8 + 5 = 13 cm.

q: Two circles of radii 10 cm and 4 cm touch internally. Find the distance between their centres.
e: Distance = r₁ - r₂ = 10 - 4 = 6 cm.

q: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. If AB = 6 cm, BC = 7 cm and CD = 4 cm, find AD. (NCERT)
e: AB + CD = BC + AD => 6 + 4 = 7 + AD => AD = 3 cm.

q: If two tangents inclined at an angle 60° are drawn to a circle of radius 3 cm, then length of each tangent is equal to: (NCERT Exemplar)
e: ∠APO = 30°. In right ΔOAP, tan 30° = 3/PA => PA = 3√3 cm.

q: Tangents PA and PB from external point P to a circle with centre O are inclined at 70°. Find ∠AOB.
A chord of a circle is 24 cm long and is at a distance of 5 cm from the centre. Find the radius of the circle.
e: Half-chord = 12 cm. Radius r = √(12² + 5²) = 13 cm.

q: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm is 6 cm away from the centre. Find the length of the chord.
e: Half-chord = √(10² - 6²) = 8 cm. Full chord = 16 cm.

q: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, if ∠A = 65°, find ∠C.
AT is a tangent at point A of a circle and AB is a chord such that ∠BAT = 50°. Find the angle ∠ACB in the alternate segment.
e: By the Alternate Segment Theorem, ∠ACB = ∠BAT = 50°.

q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle. If PA = 9 cm, find PB.
e: Lengths of tangents from an external point are equal: PB = PA = 9 cm.

q: The length of tangent PT from a point P at 10 cm from centre O is 8 cm. Find the diameter of the circle.
e: Radius r = √(10² - 8²) = 6 cm. Diameter = 2r = 12 cm.

q: Tangents PA and PB from P to a circle of radius 4 cm are inclined at 60°. Find the distance OP.
A circle is inscribed in ΔABC touching AB, BC, CA at P, Q, R respectively. If AP = 4 cm, BP = 5 cm and CQ = 6 cm, find the perimeter of ΔABC.
e: Perimeter = 2(AP + BP + CQ) = 2(4 + 5 + 6) = 30 cm.

q: Two concentric circles have radii 13 cm and 5 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle touching the smaller circle.
e: Half-chord = √(13² - 5²) = 12 cm. Full chord = 24 cm.

q: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. What angle does the tangent drawn at B make with AB?
e: Diameter lies along the radius OB, which is perpendicular (90°) to the tangent at B.

q: Two chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle at P. If AP = 6 cm, PB = 4 cm and CP = 8 cm, find PD.
e: AP × PB = CP × PD => 24 = 8 × PD => PD = 3 cm.

q: From external point A, tangent AB = 6 cm and secant ACD with AC = 4 cm are drawn to a circle. Find CD.
In right ΔABC with AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and ∠B = 90°, find the radius of the incircle of ΔABC.
e: AC = 10 cm. Inradius of right triangle = (8 + 6 - 10)/2 = 2 cm.

q: TP and TQ are two tangents from T to a circle with centre O. If ∠PTQ = 50°, find ∠OPQ. (NCERT)
If an arc AB subtends ∠AOB = 80° at the centre O, find ∠ACB at a point C on the major arc.
e: ∠ACB = ½ ∠AOB = 40°.

q: PQ is a chord of length 8 cm of a circle of radius 5 cm. The tangents at P and Q intersect at a point T. Find the length TP. (NCERT)
e: OT bisects chord PQ perpendicularly at R, so PR = 4 cm and OR = √(5² - 4²) = 3 cm. From ΔOPT ~ ΔORP, TP/4 = 5/3 => TP = 20/3 cm.

q: A triangle ABC is drawn to circumscribe a circle of radius 4 cm such that segments BD and DC into which BC is divided by point of contact D are 8 cm and 6 cm respectively. Find side AB. (NCERT)
e: Let AE = AF = x. Equating r·s = √[s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)] gives 4(x+14) = √[(x+14)(14-something)...] => 48x(x+14) = 16(x+14)² => 3x = x+14 => x = 7 cm. So AB = 7 + 8 = 15 cm.

q: In the same NCERT problem (r = 4 cm, BD = 8 cm, DC = 6 cm), find the length of side AC. (NCERT)
e: With x = 7 cm, AC = 7 + 6 = 13 cm.

q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from P to a circle. Another tangent CD touches the circle at E and meets PA, PB at C, D. If PA = 12 cm, find the perimeter of ΔPCD. (CBSE PYQ)
e: Perimeter(ΔPCD) = PA + PB = 12 + 12 = 24 cm (since CE = CA and DE = DB).

q: In right ΔABC (∠B = 90°), AB = 12 cm and BC = 5 cm. Find the radius of its inscribed circle. (CBSE PYQ)
e: AC = 13 cm. Inradius r = (12 + 5 - 13)/2 = 2 cm.

q: A circle inscribed in ΔABC touches sides AB, BC, CA at F, D, E respectively. If AB = 10 cm, BC = 8 cm and AC = 12 cm, find the length AF (from A to the point of contact on AB).
e: Semi-perimeter s = (10 + 8 + 12)/2 = 15 cm. Tangent segment AF = s - BC = 15 - 8 = 7 cm.

q: In the same triangle (AB = 10 cm, BC = 8 cm, AC = 12 cm), find the tangent lengths BF and CD respectively.
A circle touches all four sides of quadrilateral PQRS. If PQ = 11 cm, QR = 12 cm and RS = 8 cm, find PS.
e: PQ + RS = QR + PS => 11 + 8 = 12 + PS => PS = 7 cm.

q: Two parallel chords AB = 16 cm and CD = 12 cm lie on opposite sides of the centre of a circle of radius 10 cm. Find the distance between the two chords.
e: d₁ = √(10² - 8²) = 6 cm; d₂ = √(10² - 6²) = 8 cm. On opposite sides, total distance = 6 + 8 = 14 cm.

q: If the same two parallel chords (16 cm and 12 cm, radius 10 cm) lay on the SAME side of the centre, what would be the distance between them?
e: On the same side, distance = 8 - 6 = 2 cm.

q: An incircle of an isosceles triangle ABC (AB = AC) touches BC at D. Which of the following is true? (NCERT)
e: AB = AC and equal tangents from A give BF = CE => BD = DC.

q: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from T. What is the relation between ∠PTQ and ∠OPQ? (NCERT Example 2)
e: Standard NCERT result: ∠PTQ = 2 ∠OPQ.

q: If two concentric circles have radii 17 cm and 8 cm, find the length of the chord of the outer circle touching the inner circle.
e: Half-chord = √(17² - 8²) = 15 cm. Full chord = 30 cm.

q: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle of radius 6 cm with ∠APB = 60°. What type of triangle is ΔPAB and what is AB?
e: PA = PB and ∠APB = 60° make ΔPAB equilateral, with AB = PA = 6 cot 30° = 6√3 cm.

q: A tangent of length 24 cm is drawn from P to a circle of radius 7 cm. What is the length of the portion of segment OP lying OUTSIDE the circle?
e: OP = √(24² + 7²) = 25 cm. Outside part = OP - r = 25 - 7 = 18 cm.

q: Vertices of ΔABC lie on a circle with ∠A = 50°. Tangents at B and C meet at P. Find ∠BPC.
e: Central angle ∠BOC = 2∠A = 100°. Thus ∠BPC = 180° - 100° = 80°.

q: XPY is a tangent at P to a circle, PR is a diameter, and chord PQ makes ∠QPY = 55°. Find ∠QRP (angle in alternate segment).
e: By Alternate Segment Theorem, ∠QRP = ∠QPY = 55°.

q: In a circle of radius 5 cm, AB = AC = 6 cm are two equal chords. Find the length of chord BC.
e: ar(ΔOAB) = ½×6×4 = 12. Using OA as base: ½×5×BM = 12 => BM = 4.8 cm => BC = 9.6 cm.

q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm. Find the radius of the inscribed circle touching all four sides.
e: Side = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm. Inradius equals altitude of each quadrant triangle: (6×8)/10 = 4.8 cm.

q: From external point P, tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle of centre O and radius 3 cm. If OP = 6 cm, find ∠APB.
If PA and PB are tangents inclined at 120° to a circle of centre O and radius 6 cm, find OP. (NCERT Optional)
A hexagon ABCDEF circumscribes a circle. If AB + CD + EF = 24 cm, find BC + DE + FA. (CBSE Important)
e: For a circumscribing hexagon, AB + CD + EF = BC + DE + FA = 24 cm.

q: Two circles touch externally at P. A direct common tangent touches them at A and B. What is ∠APB always equal to? (CBSE PYQ)
e: The common tangent at P meets AB at T with TA = TP = TB, making P lie on the semicircle with diameter AB, so ∠APB = 90°.

q: From external point P, tangents PQ and PR to a circle of radius 5 cm make ∠QPR = 90°. Find PQ.
e: OQPR has all angles 90° and OQ = OR = 5 cm, so it is a square of side 5 cm => PQ = 5 cm.

q: O is the centre of a circle of radius OA = 9 cm and PA is a tangent. If ∠POA = 60°, find PA.
e: In right ΔOAP (∠OAP = 90°), tan 60° = PA/OA => PA = 9√3 cm.

q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from P (25 cm from centre O) to a circle of radius 7 cm. Find the area of quadrilateral OAPB.
e: PA = 24 cm. Area(OAPB) = 2 × (½ × 7 × 24) = 168 cm².

q: The sides of a triangle are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. Find the radius of its inscribed circle.
e: s = 21 cm. Area = √(21×8×7×6) = 84 cm². Inradius r = Area / s = 84 / 21 = 4 cm.

q: A rectangle of sides 12 cm and 5 cm is inscribed in a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
e: Diagonal = diameter = √(12² + 5²) = 13 cm => radius = 6.5 cm.

q: Two circles of radii 9 cm and 4 cm have centres 13 cm apart (touching externally). Find the length of their direct common tangent.
e: Length = √(d² - (r₁ - r₂)²) = √(13² - 5²) = 12 cm.

q: A tangent PT at point P on a circle meets a line through centre O at T such that OT = 10 cm and ∠PTO = 30°. Find the radius of the circle.
e: ∠OPT = 90° => OP = OT sin 30° = 5 cm.

q: [Case Study 1] The centre O of a Ferris wheel (radius 9 m) is at a height/distance OP = 15 m from an anchor point P on the ground. Anchor cables PA and PB touch the wheel tangentially at A and B. What is the measure of ∠OAP?
e: Angle between radius OA and tangent PA at the point of contact is 90°.

q: [Case Study 1 contd.] If OP = 15 m and radius OA = 9 m, what is the length of each tangent cable PA?
[Case Study 1 contd.] How does the length of cable PB compare with PA?
e: Tangents from an external point are equal, so PB = PA = 12 m.

q: [Case Study 1 contd.] What is the total area of the quadrilateral OAPB?
[Case Study 1 contd.] If the two points of contact A and B are connected by a straight rod AB, what is the length of AB?
[Case Study 2] A circular pond is inscribed in a triangular park PQR touching sides PQ, QR, RP at A, B, C respectively. If PQ = 12 m, QR = 8 m and RP = 10 m, find the semi-perimeter (s) of ΔPQR.
[Case Study 2 contd.] Find the distance PA from vertex P to the point of contact A on PQ.
[Case Study 2 contd.] Find the lengths QB and RC respectively.
[Case Study 2 contd.] If the area of ΔPQR (sides 12, 8, 10 m) is 15√7 m², find the radius of the circular pond.
[Case Study 2 contd.] How are the two segments PA and PC from vertex P related?
e: By Theorem 10.2, tangents from vertex P to the circle are equal: PA = PC.

q: Two parallel tangents XY and X'Y' of a circle with centre O are intersected by another tangent AB (point of contact C) at A and B. What is the measure of ∠AOB? (NCERT)
e: OA and OB bisect ∠POC and ∠QOC respectively; since ∠POC + ∠QOC = 180°, ∠AOB = 90°.

q: In the above NCERT setup (∠AOB = 90°, OC ⊥ AB), if radius OC = 6 cm and AC = 4 cm, find BC.
e: In right ΔAOB with OC ⊥ AB, OC² = AC · BC => 36 = 4 · BC => BC = 9 cm.

q: Two concentric circles have radii 10 cm and 6 cm. A tangent PT is drawn from a point P on the outer circle to the inner circle. Find PT.
A right triangle has legs a, b, inradius r and circumradius R. What does a + b equal?
e: Since c = 2R and 2r = a + b - c, we get a + b = 2(R + r).

q: A circle touches side BC of ΔABC at P and touches AB and AC produced at Q and R respectively. If the perimeter of ΔABC is 28 cm, find AQ. (CBSE PYQ)
e: Standard theorem: AQ = ½ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 28/2 = 14 cm.

q: If two circles of radii 4 cm and 1 cm touch externally, find the length of their direct common tangent.
In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠B = 90° and a circle touches AB, BC, CD, DA at P, Q, R, S respectively. If AD = 23 cm, AB = 29 cm and DS = 5 cm, find the radius of the circle. (CBSE PYQ)
e: AS = 23 - 5 = 18 cm => AP = 18 cm => PB = 29 - 18 = 11 cm. Since ∠B = 90°, OPBQ is a square, so r = PB = 11 cm.

q: In quadrilateral ABCD with ∠D = 90°, a circle touches AB, BC, CD, DA at P, Q, R, S respectively. If BC = 38 cm, CD = 25 cm and BP = 27 cm, find the radius of the circle.
From point P at distance OP from centre O of a circle of radius r, two tangents PA and PB make ∠APB = 60°. What is OP : r?
Two chords AB and CD intersect perpendicularly at E inside a circle. If AE = 4 cm, EB = 6 cm, CE = 3 cm and ED = 8 cm, find the diameter of the circle. (HOTS)
e: For perpendicular chords, diameter² = AE² + EB² + CE² + ED² = 16 + 36 + 9 + 64 = 125 => d = 5√5 cm.

q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from P to a circle of centre O and radius 10 cm. If chord of contact AB = 16 cm, find PA.
e: AM = 8, OM = 6. From ΔOAP ~ ΔOMA, PA/8 = 10/6 => PA = 40/3 cm.

q: Three circles of radii 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm touch each other externally. Find the perimeter of the triangle formed by joining their centres.
e: Sides are 5, 7, 6 cm. Perimeter = 2(2 + 3 + 4) = 18 cm.

q: If three circles of radii 1 cm, 2 cm and 3 cm touch each other externally, what type of triangle is formed by joining their centres?
e: Sides are 3, 4, 5 cm. Since 3² + 4² = 5², it is a right-angled triangle!

q: What is the area of the largest square inscribed in a circle of radius 10 cm?
e: Diagonal = diameter = 20 cm. Area = ½ × 20² = 200 cm².

q: What is the ratio of the area of a square circumscribing a circle to that of a square inscribed in the same circle?
e: Outer square area = (2r)² = 4r²; inner square area = ½(2r)² = 2r². Ratio = 2 : 1.

q: In ΔABC, if an incircle has centre I and ∠A = 80°, what is ∠BIC?
Tangents PA and PB are drawn from P to a circle of centre O and radius r. If chord AB subtends 120° at O, find OP.
Secants PAB and PCD meet outside a circle at P (P-B-A and P-D-C). If PA = 12 cm, PB = 4 cm and PD = 6 cm, find PC.
e: PA · PB = PC · PD => 12 × 4 = PC × 6 => PC = 8 cm.

q: What is always true about the non-parallel sides of a cyclic trapezium?
e: Every cyclic trapezium is isosceles, so its non-parallel sides are equal.

q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from P (OP = 12 cm) to a circle of radius OA = 6 cm. Find ∠AOB and OM (where OP cuts AB at M) respectively.
Tangents PA and PB from P satisfy AB = PA = PB = 6 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
e: ΔPAB is equilateral so ∠APB = 60° => ∠APO = 30°. r = 6 tan 30° = 2√3 cm.

q: From centre O of a circle of radius 13 cm, the perpendicular distance to chord PQ is OM = 5 cm. Find sin θ where θ is the acute angle between tangent PT at P and chord PQ.
e: ∠OPT = 90° => ∠OPQ = 90° - θ. In right ΔOMP, PM = 12 cm, so sin θ = cos(∠OPQ) = PM/OP = 12/13.

q: Each side of an equilateral triangle is 6√3 cm. Find its inradius and circumradius respectively.
e: Altitude h = (√3/2)(6√3) = 9 cm. Inradius r = h/3 = 3 cm and circumradius R = 2h/3 = 6 cm.

q: A, B, C, D lie in order on a circle with diameter AD. If ∠ABC = 130°, find ∠CAD.
e: ∠ADC = 180° - 130° = 50°. Since AD is diameter, ∠ACD = 90°, so ∠CAD = 90° - 50° = 40°.

q: The radii of two circles are 15 cm and 7 cm, and the distance between their centres is 17 cm. Find the length of their direct common tangent.
Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm have centres 10 cm apart. Find the length of their transverse common tangent.
e: Transverse tangent length = √(d² - (r₁ + r₂)²) = √(10² - 8²) = 6 cm.

q: A and B lie on a circle of centre O and radius r such that ∠AOB = 90°. Tangents at A and B meet at P. Find ar(ΔPAB).
e: OAPB is a square of side r, so PA = PB = r and ∠APB = 90°, giving area = r²/2.

q: If a semicircle is drawn on hypotenuse BC of right ΔABC (∠A = 90°) as diameter, it must pass through:
e: Since ∠BAC = 90°, by converse of Thales/semicircle theorem, A lies on the semicircle.

q: Tangents PA and PB from P are inclined at 80°. Point Q lies on the major arc AB. Find ∠AQB.
e: ∠AOB = 100°, so inscribed angle ∠AQB = 100°/2 = 50°.

q: If the inradius of ΔABC is 3 cm and its perimeter is 24 cm, find the area of ΔABC.
e: Area = r × s = 3 × 12 = 36 cm².
